The 0x30 Matrix4x3 struct copy in func_ov029_02112250 matches without the array-wrapper lever (the flat m[12] spelling is in scope here). SUPERSEDED IN PART by the promotion: this note used to add `duplicate real destructor collapsed; +8 at the Spawn`, and both are now false. The single real ~daObjWc_Mizu_c() member was replaced by two `// @symbol` mangled bodies (see the next note), and classInit's `&_ZTV14daObjWc_Mizu_c[2]` became a plain addend-0 reference to the same symbol.

PROMOTION (this is the note to read first). Two conditions had to be settled. (1) EMISSION ORDER. The cartridge keeps D1 at 0x021121a4, BELOW D0 at 0x021121f0, while a real `daObjWc_Mizu_c::~daObjWc_Mizu_c()` member makes mwccarm emit the D2/D1/D0 triple as one group in the order D0-then-D1; objisolate refuses that with `requested functions are not emitted in ROM order` and the group also carries an unhomed D2. Both variants are therefore written as separate `// @symbol` bodies under their mangled names in src/game/actors/d_a_obj_wc_mizu.cpp, read off the cartridge with tools/disasm.py (ov029 base 0x021111a0). That costs the CONVERTED tier's no-raw-offset and no-mangled-refs criteria for those two functions, banked in config/converted-backslide-exceptions.jsonl. This manifest's `functions_occur_in_expected_order: PARTIAL -- [(0, 1)]` was the advance warning; it now reads PASS. (2) NO VPTR BIAS. symbols.txt records _ZTV14daObjWc_Mizu_c at 0x021140dc and that IS the address point -- the cartridge's literal pool word at 0x021121e8 is exactly 0x021140dc -- so every vptr store names the symbol with addend 0. The former `&_ZTV14daObjWc_Mizu_c[2]` spelling is refused by production isolation with `intact multi-symbol object has undefined RTTI addend 8; text-only production isolation cannot rewrite it`.

WHY THE DESTRUCTOR IS DECLARED LAST IN include/daObjWc_Mizu_c.h, and where the 11 compiler_only_output entries come from. Nothing defines ~daObjWc_Mizu_c() as a C++ member (see the previous note), so the class's vtable and RTTI have no key function to home them. Whether mwccarm then emits them here at all turns on WHERE the destructor is declared inside the class: measured on this class, with `virtual ~daObjWc_Mizu_c();` declared FIRST the TU emits 0 data symbols; moved AFTER the four non-virtual methods it emits 11 (6 VERIFIED, 5 PARTIAL against the cartridge). include/daObjWc_Obj04_c.h already had the dtor last, which is why the sibling licenses 11 and this one appeared not to need any. The first shape is not harmless: it drops _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV14daObjWc_Mizu_c out of the set of ROM data any source verifies, and tools/validate_merge.py ratchets on that count (`ROM data verified from source fell from 604 to 603 symbol(s)` on pull request #2184). With the dtor declared last the count is 605. Proved by tools/rombuild.py -j16 at 106/106 exact, mismatching 0.

LEFTOVER CLEANUP. SUPERSEDES the two previous notes' destructor-form claims. classInit is now `return new daObjWc_Mizu_c()` with a leaf `operator new(unsigned long)` forwarding `_ZN7fBase_cnwEj((unsigned)size)`. `virtual ~daObjWc_Mizu_c() {}` is inline and first in the class, so mwccarm emits the retail D1-then-D0 pair and no leaf D2; InitResources is the key function and still homes _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS here (deadstrip-data, same 11 records).
